newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse closes firmer after U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse closes firmer after U.S. election.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse ended sharply higher on Wednesday after Bill Clinton held onto the U.S. Presidency and the Republicans maintained control of Congress, a combination markets saw as optimal.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares, closed up 37.90 points, or 1.41 percent at 2,729.19, but off the day's highs and below the all-time bourse high of 2,739.26 hit on October 18.
Although the U.S. election results provided the main focus, the market was also kept busy digesting a barrage of company figures and news.

Chemical company Hoechst ended trade above the critical 60 mark level for the first time, up 2.27 marks, or almost four percent, at 60.10 marks, after the company's nine month results were well received.
Competing chemical companies BASF AG and Bayer AG were pulled up by Hoechst's success. BASF ended bourse dealings up 1.33 marks at 50.87 marks, while Bayer climbed 1.27 marks to 58.65 marks.
Preference shares in business software group SAP AG gained the most ground amongst the DAX stocks, continuing to recover from the blow of a profit warning two weeks ago.
SAP preference shares ended bourse dealings up over five percent, or 10.70 marks, at 206.70 marks.

Industrial group Daimler Benz AG also climbed strongly, after a newsletter said the firm was due to report nine-month turnover growth of 10 percent on Thursday. Daimler ended floor trade up 1.64 marks at 92.69 marks.
Truck manufacturing and engineering group MAN AG was the only DAX stock to end bourse trade lower, down five marks, at 3696.00 marks after the firm announced a rise in July to September sales.

Electronics firm Siemens, which had gained one percent to end bourse trade up at 80.20 marks, tumbled in computer dealings after the company announced 1995/96 results and said it saw no improvement in results for the 1996/97 financial year.
